result:
Compilation succeeded. I've created three self-contained JUnit 5 test classes under `tests/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/`:

- **`FastDateFormatAgentTest`** — covers all `getInstance`/`getDateInstance`/`getTimeInstance`/`getDateTimeInstance` factories, the protected constructors (null-argument `NullPointerException`, century-start 2-digit-year resolution), every `format` overload (millis/Date/Calendar, `Appendable`, deprecated `StringBuffer`, `Object`+`FieldPosition`, unsupported-type `IllegalArgumentException`), all `parse`/`parseObject` overloads (success, failure, error index), `getMaxLengthEstimate`, the documented defensive copy from `getTimeZone()`, `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`, and `clear()`.
- **`FastDatePrinterAgentTest`** — constructed directly via the package-accessible protected constructor; covers NPE on null args, all `format` overloads including the package-private `format(Object)` and deprecated `format(Object,StringBuffer,FieldPosition)`, the printer-time-zone-wins-over-calendar-time-zone behavior, `getTimeZoneDisplay`, `parsePattern` (valid/invalid pattern), `selectNumberRule`, `parseToken`, `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`, and `clear()`.
- **`FastDateParserAgentTest`** — constructed via the protected constructors; covers the null-locale-defaults-to-system-locale behavior, documented lenient-mode minute rollover, all `parse`/`parseObject` overloads (including the documented "error index before the failed field" behavior and the non-lenient `Calendar` `IllegalArgumentException`), `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`/`toStringAll`, `clear()`, `getPatterns()`, and the `JAPANESE_IMPERIAL` field.

Every assertion is tied to a statement in the javadoc under `api/`; where the javadoc was silent on exact mechanics (e.g., `parseToken`/`selectNumberRule` internals), I only asserted the type-safe, implied properties rather than guessing internals. `./compile.sh` reports `compiled OK`.
